documentTitle: EASA Private Pilot Studies -- Chapter 12 Communications

sections.title: Communications introduction, radio discipline, frequency basics
sections.notes: Useful as training/background context for standard phraseology, concise transmissions, listening watch, frequency expression, 8.33 kHz capability wording, and primary-reference pointers.

sections.title: Q codes and categories of message
sections.notes: Low priority for ingestion because primary regulatory and phraseology sources already cover urgency/distress and message priority more directly.

sections.title: Operating procedures, standard words, callsigns, and time
sections.notes: Contains useful pilot-training coverage of transmission technique, initial calls, ATIS mention on first contact, standard words/phrases, time expression, and callsign abbreviation cautions.

sections.title: Aeronautical stations, service suffixes, and position reports
sections.notes: Useful background for station/service suffixes, position-report item order, and pilot-side sequencing of ATIS, startup, taxi, joining, circuit reports, and go-around calls.

sections.title: Ground, tower, circuit, approach, and radar-service background
sections.notes: Useful as background for ground/tower responsibilities, taxi clearance limits, circuit/final reporting, continue versus landing clearance, and approach/radar service context.

sections.title: Clearances, readbacks, conditional clearances, radio checks, and transfer
sections.notes: Most relevant EPPLS window: pilot-side readback expectations, clearance/instruction distinction, conditional-clearance sequence, test-transmission format, readability scale, and transfer-of-communication examples.

sections.title: Radio failure
sections.notes: Useful background for aircraft-side communications-failure checks, transmitting-blind technique, last-clearance compliance, circuit light signals, receiver-failure reports, and transponder code context.

sections.title: Distress and urgency
sections.notes: Useful background for distress/urgency message shape, radio silence, cancellation, emergency frequencies, fuel-emergency wording, and emergency transponder code context. Primary sources remain H01, ICAO, SERA, and CAP 413.

sections.title: Propagation, frequencies, and interception
sections.notes: Not worth ingesting in this close-out; it is a short cross-reference to other training material with little source-unit value for FN10.

summary.overallDisposition: Chapter 12 has ingest-worthy material, but only as background/training support.
